project.title: When Governance Changes What Gets Counted: Measurement Validity for LLM Agent Evaluation

contract.gap: Runtime governance evaluations can use a condition written by the agent both to enforce a rule and to select the records used by a conditional rate.
contract.task: Evaluate this measurement-validity risk with paired WAGF simulations and define a reporting protocol that keeps the denominator and world-state dependence visible.
outcomes: share of decisions with the agent-written scarcity condition

questions.text: Does enforcement change the share of decisions with an agent-reported condition as well as the rate computed among those decisions?
How much of the anchor contrast is descriptively associated with different simulator-recorded world states?
Which additional statistics remain interpretable when the same denominator is used by design?

contract.contribution: A bounded measurement-validity risk and a minimal reporting protocol for governed LLM-agent evaluations.
nonclaims: The paper does not claim deception or gaming.
The paper does not identify a causal effect of validation.
The paper does not identify a within-world reporting revision because the first response before retry is missing.
The paper does not claim universal behavior across agent frameworks.
The paper does not treat reweighting as a causal adjustment or corrected effect estimate.

alignment.method: Compare validator-on and validator-off condition shares and conditional rates in paired irrigation simulations.
alignment.evidence: Table 1 and the frozen irrigation evidence inventory report per-seed values and contrasts.
alignment.result: All five irrigation configurations have positive condition-share contrasts; the anchor executed conditional rate contrast is +25.90 percentage points.
alignment.interpretation: The conditional score and its selected population move together.
alignment.limitation: The first response before a retry is unavailable, so within-decision report revision is unresolved.
alignment.contribution: Shows why a conditional conformance score needs the condition share beside it.

alignment.method: Directly standardize the condition share to pooled simulator-recorded world-state distributions in the anchor irrigation cell.
alignment.evidence: Figure 3 panels A--B and the frozen world-state evidence files report pooled differences, coverage, and per-seed diagnostics.
alignment.result: The pooled difference is -2.53 percentage points at full coverage and +0.21 at the finest reported grouping.
alignment.interpretation: Different recorded-world composition is consistent with much of the raw condition-share contrast.
alignment.limitation: World state is downstream of governance, so the decomposition is descriptive rather than causal.
alignment.contribution: Separates a supported world-state composition diagnosis from an unsupported causal claim.

alignment.method: Compare the executed conditional increase rate with the executed all-decision rate, and retain the final-proposal reading only as sensitivity.
alignment.evidence: Figure 4 and the frozen consequence evidence report contrasts for all five irrigation configurations.
alignment.result: Executed all-decision contrasts range from +20.26 to +36.57 percentage points; the conditional-minus-all gap ranges from -14.86 to +3.38, with four negative and one positive gap.
alignment.interpretation: The denominator is part of the estimand, not a formatting detail.
alignment.limitation: The all-decision rate answers a different question and is not presented as an automatic correction.
alignment.contribution: Provides a minimal reporting protocol for governed-agent evaluations.

decisions.decision: Use ICLR 2027 as the active release target; retain AAMAS 2027 as a fallback after the ICLR decision or withdrawal.

Use generated shared-condition v6 with a subordinate retry/default-action branch: a compact Agent response card, explicit black and amber Validator ports, a final-record route to Decision log, black borders with flat colored fills, a direct condition-to-Counted-records route, and a retry arrow that returns to Agent response.
decisions.authority: AGENT_ARCHITECTURE_FIGURE_RESET.md, FIGURE1_DESIGN.md, and current visual review

decisions.decision: Use the executed action as the primary reading; retain the final-proposal/last-proposed reading only as an explicit sensitivity analysis.

Treat validator-on versus validator-off as the object reported by governed-agent evaluations and audited by this paper, not as an estimator of a governance effect; governance changes the recorded world by design.

Describe high_threat_high_cope_no_increase as a testbed policy branch: it blocks increase proposals only for high/very-high scarcity together with high/very-high coping; high scarcity alone warns rather than blocks.

Retain nine Flood configurations as a secondary cross-testbed boundary check in Table 2 and the cross-testbed summary; do not promote them to a same-status mechanism panel. Exclude the one divergent governed B6 run and disclose the sensitivity. Report the corrected 0--0.638% Flood rejection-pressure range from the live handoff.
decisions.authority: ICLR2027/flood_control_contrasts.csv, source/cross_testbed_summary.py, and current Cloud handoff
